hero.subtitle: Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame of the 12S rRNA-c · 16 amino acids
hero.short_description: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide (MRWQEMGYIFYPRKLR) encoded within the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene, listed in reference databases as mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c. Veracue supplies it as a research material for laboratory work. The most directly relevant published study (Lee et al., 2015) tested MOTS-c in cultured cells and diet-induced obese mice — cell-culture and animal evidence only. A Phase 2a human trial (NCT07505745) is currently recruiting, so this material does not yet establish metabolic, exercise or safety effects in people.
hero.intro: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide encoded by a short open reading frame inside the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene. Its discovery in 2015 drew attention for a simple reason: it suggested that mitochondria can signal to the cell with peptides from their own genome. Since then, researchers have studied it in cells and mice, mainly for metabolic signaling, AMPK and stress responses. For a peptide of this size, identity is not a formality. In particular, two oxidation-prone methionines and an arginine-rich sequence make analytical documentation central to any study. Accordingly, Veracue supplies MOTS-c strictly for laboratory research use.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: MOTS-c stands for mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c. The name describes where the sequence sits. It lies inside the gene for the smaller ribosomal RNA of human mitochondria, a stretch of DNA long assumed to encode RNA only. Lee and colleagues then reported the peptide in Cell Metabolism in 2015, following the earlier discovery of humanin in the neighboring 16S rRNA gene.

Most researchers meet MOTS-c through metabolic biology. The founding paper tied it to skeletal muscle, the folate cycle and AMPK. After that, later studies examined nuclear gene regulation and exercise. That literature is genuinely interesting; however, it is narrower than online summaries suggest. This page therefore separates what researchers measured in cells, in mice and in people.

sections.heading: Intended Use
paragraphs: Veracue offers this material for in vitro and laboratory research. Typical examples include cell-culture work on mitochondrial signaling, AMPK and stress-response pathways, or analytical method development for mid-sized basic peptides. It is not a drug, supplement, food or cosmetic. Likewise, it is not intended for administration to humans or animals.
Research-use positioning is more than a label. For that reason, nothing on this page provides, or should be read as, dosing, administration, reconstitution-for-use or treatment information.

sections.heading: What Is MOTS-c Peptide?
paragraphs: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide (MRWQEMGYIFYPRKLR) encoded within the mitochondrial genome, in a short open reading frame of the 12S rRNA gene. It belongs to a small group called mitochondrial-derived peptides, alongside humanin and the small humanin-like peptides. Researchers study it because it points to a less familiar role for mitochondria: producing signaling molecules, not only energy.

The founding 2015 study linked MOTS-c to the folate cycle, de novo purine synthesis and AMPK activation in cultured cells, and reported metabolic effects in mice. Later work then described its movement into the nucleus under cellular stress. Importantly, these are laboratory and animal findings. However, human studies so far have mainly measured the body's own MOTS-c, so no study has established a human outcome for administered MOTS-c.

subsections.heading: Molecular Identity and Structure
paragraphs: MOTS-c is a linear peptide of 16 L-amino acids with a free amine at one end and a free carboxylic acid at the other. Notably, three arginines and a lysine, set against a single glutamate, give it a strongly basic character. In addition, two methionines (positions 1 and 6) and a tryptophan (position 3) are the residues most prone to oxidation. These features matter more at the bench than in a textbook, because they shape how the peptide behaves in chromatography, mass spectrometry and storage.

subsections.heading: Mitochondrial Research Context
paragraphs: Human mitochondrial DNA carries 37 genes: 13 for proteins, 22 for transfer RNAs and 2 for ribosomal RNAs. Humanin, reported in 2001 from the 16S rRNA region, showed that short open reading frames can hide inside those RNA genes. Building on that finding, Lee and colleagues reported MOTS-c from the 12S rRNA region in 2015.

subsections.heading: Metabolic and Cellular Signaling Research
paragraphs: In the 2015 study, MOTS-c inhibited the folate cycle and the de novo purine pathway tethered to it. As a result, the purine intermediate AICAR accumulated and AMPK became active. The authors proposed this route as partly responsible for the effects they saw. Meanwhile, skeletal muscle appeared to be the main target tissue. In mice, MOTS-c treatment prevented diet-induced obesity and both diet- and age-dependent insulin resistance.

A 2018 study then reported that, under metabolic stress in cultured cells, MOTS-c moved into the nucleus in an AMPK-dependent manner. Once there, it interacted with stress-responsive transcription factors such as NRF2 and regulated genes carrying antioxidant response elements.

subsections.heading: What the Evidence Actually Establishes
paragraphs: Taken together, the literature establishes a defined molecule, a mechanistic model and a set of mouse observations. It does not establish a human effect. Human studies have mostly measured endogenous MOTS-c. For example, levels rose in muscle and plasma during a cycling session in young men. In an ageing cohort, by contrast, plasma levels were lower in older men while muscle expression was higher. That split between tissues shows how much MOTS-c biology depends on where, and how, researchers measure it.

sections.heading: What Does MOTS-c Peptide Do?
paragraphs: In research terms, experimental studies have investigated MOTS-c in relation to four connected processes. In cultured cells, it inhibited the folate cycle and the linked purine pathway, which raised AICAR and activated AMPK, the cell's energy-sensing kinase. Similarly, under glucose restriction and oxidative stress, it entered the nucleus and influenced stress-responsive genes. In mice, treatment altered glucose handling and diet-related weight gain and, in a later study, physical performance at young, middle and old ages. Even so, what MOTS-c does in an intact human body remains an open question.

sections.heading: What Is MOTS-c Used For in Research?
paragraphs: Researchers use MOTS-c as a tool to study mitochondrial-to-nuclear signaling, folate metabolism and purine synthesis. In addition, it helps probe AMPK signaling and cellular responses to glucose restriction and oxidative stress. It also appears in rodent studies of skeletal-muscle metabolism and physical capacity, and in cell work on myoblast adaptation to metabolic stress. Human cohort studies, meanwhile, measure naturally occurring MOTS-c in exercise and ageing research. In every case, the application is a research question, not a use in people.

sections.heading: MOTS-c Peptide Benefits: What the Research Has Investigated
paragraphs: Searches for MOTS-c peptide benefits usually expect a list. However, the honest answer is a table. Each row below names the question a study asked, the system it used and what it did not show. Above all, experimental activity in cells or mice is not the same as a benefit in people, and no row here should be read that way.

sections.heading: Common MOTS-c Misattributions
list: Many pages credit nuclear translocation to the 2015 paper. In fact, Kim and colleagues reported it in 2018.
Some pages say MOTS-c depletes or reduces AICAR. The 2015 study reported the opposite: AICAR accumulated.
Online summaries often present the insulin-sensitivity findings as human results. They came from mice.
Exercise data are sometimes described as MOTS-c improving human endurance. The human data tracked the body's own MOTS-c rising during exercise; the performance effects came from mice.
'MOTS-c declines with age' is only half the picture. In men, plasma levels were lower with age while muscle expression was higher.

sections.heading: MOTS-c Side Effects
paragraphs: Human safety and adverse-event guidance for MOTS-c is outside the scope of this Research Use Only page, so this page gives none. Safety observations in the literature belong to specific designs — a cell line, a mouse strain, a formulation, a duration. Consequently, they cannot simply carry over to people. Instead, in the laboratory, handle MOTS-c as a research chemical, following the safety documentation supplied with the lot and your institution's procedures. This page is not medical advice.

sections.heading: MOTS-c Dosage and Dosing Protocols
paragraphs: Human dosage guidance for MOTS-c is outside the scope of this Research Use Only product page. This page gives no daily, weekly, per-cycle or 'protocol' figures. Amounts in animal studies depend on species, formulation, route and endpoint; they are not conversions for people.

For study design, the useful questions are different. Which published model matches your question? Which vehicle and pathway controls does it need? Does the documentation confirm the lot's identity and net peptide content, so that concentrations reflect peptide rather than salt and water? Finally, recording the lot number with every experiment makes results traceable and reproducible.

sections.heading: Why There Is No MOTS-c Dosage Chart
paragraphs: A dosage chart would present human-use instructions for a material that is not intended for human use. Therefore this page does not provide one, in any unit. Instead, researchers who need the amounts used in a particular model should read that study's methods section directly. It also describes how the authors prepared and characterized their peptide.

sections.heading: MOTS-c Tablets and Oral Forms
paragraphs: This listing is a research material, not a tablet, capsule, supplement or food. Questions about oral products, formulation or route of administration in people fall outside the scope of this page, so it offers no such guidance.

sections.heading: MOTS-c vs Related Research Compounds
paragraphs: People often search for MOTS-c alongside compounds it has little in common with. Humanin is its closest relative: another mitochondrial-derived peptide, from the 16S rRNA gene. SS-31, by contrast, is a synthetic tetrapeptide designed to bind cardiolipin, not a peptide encoded by mitochondria. Meanwhile, NAD+ and AICAR are not peptides at all. Retatrutide and tesamorelin act on cell-surface receptors, whereas MOTS-c research centers on intracellular metabolic pathways. For clarity, the tables below compare them on identity and research context only.

subsections.heading: RP-HPLC
paragraphs: Reversed-phase HPLC reports how much of the detected signal falls in the main peak under stated conditions. For MOTS-c, the method details matter. Detection near 214–220 nm reports peptide bonds, while tryptophan and tyrosine also absorb near 280 nm, so the wavelength changes relative responses. HPLC does not establish identity, counterion, water content or net peptide content, and closely related variants can co-elute with the main peak.

subsections.heading: Mass Spectrometry
paragraphs: Mass spectrometry tests whether the observed mass is consistent with MOTS-c. Because the peptide carries four basic side chains, electrospray spectra usually show several charge states. A COA should state whether it reports monoisotopic or average mass, since mixing them creates an apparent 1.5 Da discrepancy. Even so, intact mass alone cannot distinguish a scrambled sequence with the same composition, and it cannot detect D-amino-acid isomers at all.
subsections.note: Reference values calculated from the sequence for identification purposes. They are not Veracue lot results.

subsections.heading: Orthogonal Methods
paragraphs: When a study depends on exact identity or concentration, additional evidence helps. Tandem MS fragmentation or Edman sequencing confirms residue order. Amino acid analysis, in turn, supports net peptide content. Counterion analysis then shows how much of the powder is trifluoroacetate or acetate. Finally, chiral amino acid analysis is the method that addresses D-isomer content.

subsections.heading: Lot-Specific Documentation
paragraphs: Analytical results only describe the lot that the laboratory tested. A purity figure from another lot says nothing certain about your vial. The same goes for a spectrum of a different peptide or a generic specification sheet. For that reason, the lot number on the COA should match the label.

sections.heading: Reading a MOTS-c Certificate of Analysis
paragraphs: A useful MOTS-c Certificate of Analysis (COA) answers four questions. What is the material? How pure is it by a named method? How much peptide is actually present? And does the report belong to your lot? Note that a generic specification sheet is not a lot-specific COA. If the MOTS-c lot COA is not listed in Veracue's Certificates archive, request it through the contact page before the material enters a study.

J_problem_research_solution.intro: Twelve research problems specific to working with MOTS-c, each with a practical approach. These describe analytical and documentation practice, not laboratory protocols or dosing.

modules.title: Confusing MOTS-c With Other Mitochondrial Peptides
modules.problem: Humanin, the small humanin-like peptides, SS-31 and MOTS-c all turn up under 'mitochondrial peptide', and product listings sometimes blur them together.
modules.research_approach: Anchor the material to origin and sequence. MOTS-c comes from the 12S rRNA gene and is 16 residues long. Humanin comes from the 16S rRNA gene and is 24 residues when translated in the cytoplasm. SS-31 is not mitochondrial-derived at all; it is a synthetic tetrapeptide, D-Arg-Dmt-Lys-Phe-NH2, designed to bind cardiolipin. Writing the full sequence next to the name in lab records keeps the mix-up out of your data.

modules.title: Relying on the Name Instead of the Sequence
modules.problem: MOTS-c, MOTS-C, MOTSc and 'mot c' all point at the same target, but a name on a label is not evidence of what is in the vial.
modules.research_approach: Treat MRWQEMGYIFYPRKLR, not the product name, as the identity of the material. Then check that the COA states the sequence, the C-terminal form and the expected mass the laboratory compared its result against. For intact-mass results, confirm the expected value matches the free-acid peptide (monoisotopic 2173.11 Da) rather than a salt or a modified variant. If the COA omits the sequence entirely, ask for it before the lot enters a study.

modules.title: Treating Purity as Proof of Identity
modules.problem: A high HPLC purity result looks decisive, yet it only says that one peak dominates under one method.
modules.research_approach: Pair chromatographic purity with an identity method. HPLC can show a clean main peak for the wrong peptide, a truncated sequence or a variant that co-elutes. Mass spectrometry, ideally with fragmentation data, ties that main peak to the MOTS-c sequence. It also helps to ask whether the laboratory measured identity on the same lot as purity. If it did not, the two results cannot vouch for each other.

modules.title: Over-Reading an HPLC Chromatogram
modules.problem: Peak area at a single UV wavelength is easy to over-interpret for a 16-residue peptide that contains tryptophan and two tyrosines.
modules.research_approach: Read the method details: column, gradient, detection wavelength and integration settings. Detection near 214–220 nm reports peptide bonds, whereas aromatic residues also absorb near 280 nm, so the choice changes relative responses. Area percentage says nothing about counterion, water or net peptide content. Finally, a chromatogram image, not just a number, makes the result checkable. It shows shoulders, baseline noise and minor peaks that a single percentage hides.

modules.title: Assigning the Mass Spectrum Correctly
modules.problem: MOTS-c carries four basic side chains, so electrospray spectra often show several charge states rather than one obvious peak.
modules.research_approach: Expect multiply charged ions: calculated [M+2H]2+ near m/z 1087.56, [M+3H]3+ near 725.38 and [M+4H]4+ near 544.28 for the free acid. A deconvoluted mass should agree with 2173.11 Da (monoisotopic) or about 2174.6 Da (average), and the COA should say which. Mixing the two produces an apparent 1.5 Da 'error' that is not real. Checking every listed charge state against the calculated values guards against misassigned peaks.

modules.title: Missing Oxidation and Deamidation Products
modules.problem: Methionines at positions 1 and 6 and a tryptophan at position 3 make MOTS-c susceptible to oxidation during synthesis, handling and storage.
modules.research_approach: Look for species at +16 Da (one methionine sulfoxide, calculated 2189.10 Da) and +32 Da (2205.10 Da); on reversed-phase HPLC these commonly elute close to the main peak. Deamidation of glutamine-4 shifts mass by about +0.98 Da and needs high-resolution data to see reliably. Recording handling conditions also lets you trace any change between aliquots back to its cause.

modules.title: Overlooking the Terminus and Counterion
modules.problem: A C-terminal amide variant sits only 0.98 Da below native MOTS-c, and salts add weight to the powder without adding peptide.
modules.research_approach: Confirm the COA specifies a free C-terminal acid, matching the native sequence, or clearly states a modification. Next, ask which counterion is present, since trifluoroacetate and acetate are both common for synthetic basic peptides. Also ask whether the laboratory measured net peptide content. Without that figure, concentrations calculated from powder weight overstate the peptide actually present, and results become harder to compare between lots.

modules.title: Transferring Literature Results to a Commercial Lot
modules.problem: Published MOTS-c studies used material prepared and characterized by specific laboratories. A new commercial lot inherits none of that characterization.
modules.research_approach: Treat each lot as a new reagent. Compare its documented sequence, form and purity with the methods sections of the papers you are building on. Where a study used a modified analog or a sequence variant, note it before comparing results. Keep the lot COA with the experimental record so reviewers can see the match. That way, a surprising result can be traced to biology rather than to an undocumented change in material.

modules.title: Expecting Findings to Repeat Across Models
modules.problem: Stressed cultured cells, metabolically challenged mice and human cohorts do not measure the same thing, so MOTS-c results differ between them.
modules.research_approach: Define the model before choosing endpoints. For example, nuclear MOTS-c regulated antioxidant-response genes in stressed cells, yet muscle MOTS-c expression in older men showed no association with those genes. Specify the cell type, stressor and timing, and state whether you measure endogenous or added peptide. Report negative results with the same care, because they help define where MOTS-c findings hold and where they do not.

modules.title: Letting a Mechanism Become an Outcome Claim
modules.problem: AMPK activation in a dish is regularly rewritten online as 'improves insulin sensitivity' in people.
modules.research_approach: Keep each claim at the level of its evidence: 'activated AMPK in cultured cells', 'prevented diet-induced insulin resistance in mice', 'rose during exercise in human muscle'. Each statement is accurate on its own. Merging them into one human benefit is not. The same discipline helps when writing up your own MOTS-c data for review. Reviewers tend to trust a result more when its claims stay inside the system that produced it.

modules.title: Comparing MOTS-c With Other Metabolic Compounds
modules.problem: Search interest pairs MOTS-c with retatrutide, tesamorelin and AICAR, but these act through different biology.
modules.research_approach: Compare on identity and mechanism class rather than outcomes. Retatrutide is a lipidated 39-residue agonist at GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. Tesamorelin is a modified 44-residue GHRH analog. AICAR is a nucleotide intermediate, which MOTS-c raised in cells, not a peptide. Each needs its own controls and analytical checks. Because the molecules differ in size, charge and modification, their COAs will look different too. This page does not address combined use.

modules.title: Building a Defensible Procurement Record
modules.problem: Months later, a reviewer may ask exactly which material produced a result, and a product name will not answer that.
modules.research_approach: File the lot-specific COA, the vial-label lot number, the date received, storage records and any in-house identity checks together. Confirm the COA's lot matches the vial and names the testing laboratory and date. If the MOTS-c lot COA is not in Veracue's Certificates archive, request it through the contact page before the material enters a study. A complete file turns a later question into a quick lookup.

blocks.a: MOTS-c peptide is a 16-amino-acid peptide, MRWQEMGYIFYPRKLR, encoded in a short open reading frame of the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene. First described in 2015, it is classed as a mitochondrial-derived peptide. Researchers study it in cell and animal models for its links to metabolic signaling, AMPK and cellular stress responses. It is supplied here for research use only.

MOTS-c is short for mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c. It is a linear peptide with the molecular formula C101H152N28O22S2 and an average molecular weight of about 2174.6 g/mol (PubChem CID 146675088). Unlike most peptides, its sequence is encoded in mitochondrial DNA rather than the nuclear genome.

In cultured cells, MOTS-c inhibited the folate cycle and linked purine synthesis, raising AICAR and activating AMPK. Under metabolic stress, it moved into the nucleus and regulated stress-response genes. In mice, it prevented diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance and enhanced physical performance. What it does in people has not been established.

MOTS-c is studied as a research tool in mitochondrial-to-nuclear signaling, folate and purine metabolism, AMPK signaling and cellular stress responses. It also appears in mouse studies of muscle metabolism and physical capacity, and in human cohort studies that measure naturally occurring MOTS-c during exercise and ageing.

No human benefit of MOTS-c has been established. Research has reported pathway effects in cultured cells (AMPK activation, nuclear gene regulation) and metabolic and physical-performance effects in mice. Human studies measured the body's own MOTS-c, not administered peptide. Experimental activity in cells or animals is not a health benefit in people.

MOTS-c is characterized by reversed-phase HPLC for chromatographic purity and mass spectrometry for identity. The expected monoisotopic mass of the free acid is 2173.11 Da, usually seen as multiply charged ions. Tandem MS confirms residue order, amino acid analysis supports net peptide content, and checks for +16 Da methionine oxidation are important.

blocks.q: What should a MOTS-c COA include?
blocks.a: A MOTS-c COA should state the product name and sequence, chemical form (terminus and counterion), lot number, testing laboratory and date, HPLC purity with the method named, and a mass result giving expected and observed values. Chromatogram and spectrum images and net peptide content add confidence. The lot must match the vial label.

blocks.q: Is MOTS-c the same as other mitochondrial peptides?
blocks.a: No. MOTS-c is a 16-residue peptide from the 12S rRNA gene. Humanin is a separate 24-residue peptide from the 16S rRNA gene, and the small humanin-like peptides come from that same region. SS-31 is a synthetic tetrapeptide that targets cardiolipin; it is not encoded by mitochondrial DNA.

blocks.q: Does Veracue provide MOTS-c dosage information?
blocks.a: No. Veracue supplies MOTS-c for laboratory research only, and human dosage information is outside the scope of its product page. No daily, weekly, protocol or chart figures are provided. Researchers designing a study should work from the primary literature for their model and from the lot's analytical documentation.

blocks.q: What does Research Use Only mean?
blocks.a: Research Use Only means a material is intended strictly for laboratory and scientific research. It is not for human or veterinary use, diagnosis or treatment, and it is not a drug, supplement or food. For MOTS-c, it means the published findings describe experiments, not uses in people.
